about.title: About me
about.text: I've been passionate about computing since my first high school programming projects, and I'm now studying computer science in Arles. I am particularly interested in programming and game development. I enjoy inventing worlds, building gameplay mechanics and solving challenges along the way.

evolution.documentTitle: From V1 to V2 | Mon Univers Informatique
evolution.title: My portfolio, from V1 to V2
evolution.intro: This website is a project in its own right. Here is my first version and how it evolved to better showcase my journey and my work.
evolution.v1text: Created in high school using the Hyperspace theme by HTML5 UP, this first version brings together an introduction, my school programming projects, my skills and a contact form. It marks my first steps with HTML structure, CSS layouts and publishing through GitHub Pages.
evolution.v1alt: The first Mon Univers Informatique website: a purple background, a sidebar menu and an introduction to Clément Dufour.
evolution.v2text: V2 introduces a dark design with purple and cyan accents. It adds project filters, French / English translation, game screenshots and a playable Blackjack demo, alongside an updated introduction.
evolution.design: Design: a new palette, project cards and previews of the actual projects.
evolution.features: Interactions: technology filters, a language switch and a game demo in the browser.
evolution.content: Content: an updated journey, featured personal projects and continued access to the first version.

fantasyHistory.documentTitle: The Fantasy: evolution and patch notes | Mon Univers Informatique
fantasyHistory.kicker: FROM THE TERMINAL TO A WEB RPG
fantasyHistory.title: The Fantasy, an evolving adventure
fantasyHistory.intro: It all began with a Python game in the terminal. Across its versions, The Fantasy has grown into a browser RPG with a campaign, skills, quests and a pixel art world.
fantasyHistory.pythonText: The original Python project is still available on GitHub. Its text interface and ASCII illustrations lay the foundations: heroes, choices, combat and experience.
fantasyHistory.pythonExcerpt: An abridged excerpt from the original French Python interface.
fantasyHistory.webTitle: The game enters a new dimension
fantasyHistory.webText: Version 2.7 builds on the RPG engine developed through previous updates and expands the visual world with characters, scenery, exploration and pixel art combat.
fantasyHistory.versionsIntro: Each stage outlines the main changes and links to the original code or documents.

v1.title: The Python beginnings
v1.summary: A text-based RPG created in high school, with its own world, choices and battles.
v1.n2: Ten hero classes, each with its own statistics and special skill.
v1.n3: Turn-based combat, enemies, bosses, events and experience-based progression.
v1.n4: An SQLite database organises classes, skills, players and enemies.

v2.title: Moving to the browser
v2.summary: The project becomes The Fantasy: The Great Adventure, with a browser-based interface.
v2.n1: The engine and interface move to JavaScript, with HTML and CSS.
v2.n2: The adventure expands to three chapters and twenty character classes.
v2.n3: Local saves, an achievement profile and settings are added.
v2.n4: Menus, enemy portraits, music and ambience support the story.

v22.title: Deeper RPG foundations
v22.summary: Combat, equipment and progression become more substantial.
v22.n1: Visible enemy intentions, damage-reducing defence and potions restored at camp.
v22.n2: Inventory with multiple item rarities, equipment and cumulative bonuses.
v22.n3: A three-path skill tree, specialisations and hero continuity between chapters.
v22.n4: Branching scenes and the cartographer quest in Chapter II.
v22.n5: Six languages, improved mobile layouts and offline interface caching through a PWA.

v23.title: Journal, quests and usability
v23.summary: The adventure becomes easier to follow, with more complete hero tracking.
v23.n1: A journal with objectives, recent decisions and a bestiary to uncover.
v23.n2: Side quests across all three chapters, choice consequences and a getting-started guide.
v23.n3: A second boss phase below 50% health and fixes for actions triggering twice.
v23.n4: A streamlined phone interface with accessible actions and on-demand panels.
v23.n5: Achievements reorganised into main objectives, a platinum achievement and class bonuses.

v24.title: A pixel art direction
v24.summary: A graphics branch prepares the characters and scenery later incorporated into 2.6.
v24.n1: Twenty distinct PNG characters: five enemies and fifteen bosses.
v24.n2: Eighteen scenery props assembled into seven environments.
v24.n3: Pixel art styling and arena compositions matched to the story locations.
v24.n4: These contributions are documented in the 2.6 merge report.
v24.source: Source: 2.4 contributions in the merge report ↗

v25.title: A skipped number
v25.summary: Version number 2.5 was not used: the history moves from 2.4 to 2.6.

v26.title: Merging gameplay and pixel art
v26.summary: The RPG engine from 2.3 meets the visual identity from 2.4.
v26.n1: Preserves the campaign, inventory, talents, quests, journal and achievements from 2.3.
v26.n2: Integrates the twenty characters and seven environments from 2.4.
v26.n3: Interface and combat adjustments keep characters and controls visible on mobile.
v26.n4: Saves, profile, settings and offline cache are specific to 2.6.

v27.title: A fuller visual world
v27.summary: The graphics update of 12 November 2026 enriches the game’s presentation.
v27.n1: Twenty classes represented by full characters in selection and on the hero sheet.
v27.n2: Fourteen backgrounds and five new sheets for weapons, equipment, adventure items, forge and village.
v27.n3: Combat backgrounds and exploration scenes matched to the current location.
v27.n4: Campaign, statistics, balance and progression rules preserved; 2.7 saves kept separate.

mancala.documentTitle: Mancala: my work on rendering | Mon Univers Informatique
mancala.title: Mancala, from board to screen
mancala.intro: A team adaptation of the strategy game Mancala. Two players choose a pit, distribute its seeds and try to collect more than their opponent.
mancala.goal: Represent a board with twelve pits and two stores, display the game state and help both players follow their turns.
mancala.role: I implemented the Pygame rendering: the board, seeds, current-player indicator and end-of-game messages.
mancala.challenge: Align the images with the board positions and clearly display seed counts that change during the game.
mancala.solution: The board and seeds are drawn on Pygame surfaces. Each pit has coordinates, with seeds arranged in small grids based on their number. The screen is redrawn to reflect the game state.
mancala.skills: Pygame 2D rendering, working with images and coordinates, element layout and visual representation of program state.
mancala.team: Clément Faure, Clément Dufour and Tom Torrente. The contribution described here is my work on rendering.
mancala.caption: The board, seeds and current-player indicator in the Python / Pygame version.

blackjack.documentTitle: Blackjack: Python and browser demo | Mon Univers Informatique
blackjack.title: Blackjack, from rules to an interactive game
blackjack.intro: A Python card game against the dealer, accompanied by a JavaScript adaptation playable directly in the portfolio.
blackjack.goal: Get as close to 21 as possible without going over, choosing to draw a card or stand while scores are calculated automatically.
blackjack.role: The Python project manages the player and dealer hands, calculates scores and responds to keyboard input. The portfolio demo adapts these principles into an independent web interface.
blackjack.challenge: Handle different game states and calculate hand values when Aces can count as either 1 or 11.
blackjack.solution: Cards and hands use lists and structured data. Totals are recalculated after each action, adjusting Ace values and resolving the dealer turn separately.
blackjack.skills: Python, lists and dictionaries, conditional logic, keyboard events and adapting game mechanics to JavaScript.
blackjack.caption: The portfolio’s JavaScript demo table, distinct from the original Python program.
blackjack.demoNote: The web demo uses simplified rules without wagers or betting. GitHub hosts the original Python / Pygame Zero project.

fantasy.goal: Grow a text-based game into a browser RPG combining story, combat, hero progression and exploration.
fantasy.role: The project brings together game mechanics, data organisation, interface work and visual integration. Its history page shows each stage of this evolution.
fantasy.challenge: Connect player choices, battles, inventory and skills while preserving coherent progression between chapters.
fantasy.solution: The JavaScript engine separates story data, game state and rendering. Local saves preserve progression, with a separate save space for each major version.
fantasy.skills: Game-state modelling, JavaScript, HTML / CSS, local saves, responsive interfaces and graphics integration.
fantasy.combat: A Chapter I battle: opponent, hero statistics and available actions.
fantasy.inventory: The inventory after the first boss loot, showing the item and its effects.
fantasy.skillsPreview: The three-path skill tree: Blade, Guardian and Alchemy.
